newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods rise more, but trade is thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods rise more, but trade is thin.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices added slightly to their morning rally late Monday, but weak fundamenetals dampened the effect of a large fire at Texaco's 96,000 bpd refinery in Wilmington, Calif..
Trade remained light, and prices failed to rally much more than two cents over their Friday levels because of weak fundamentals.
"Because of (California's) low rack prices and low retail prices, the bids never came in," one trader said.
Bids for CARB-grade gasoline in Los Angeles added another penny to their 0.75-cent rise this morning, touching 64 cents a gallon. Offers rose to 65 cents.
Meanwhile, conventional unleaded climbed another cent to 60/61 cents a gallon.
Diesel fuels remained unchanged at mornings levels. Low sulphur hung at 67.50/68.50 cents a gallon.
Traders said Texaco stayed out of the spot market, choosing to borrow fuel from other major oil companies.
"They'll take as much help as they can from other majors," a broker said.
